decisions.reason: As a multi-model system built on the firm’s established offer, it carries enough sunk cost and managerial commitment to be kept despite being less central than design-led interior flooring.

Even with escalation pressure from the investment in a full product line, a mobile arena system is peripheral to the firm’s stated trend-led interior strategy and therefore becomes a plausible candidate for withdrawal.

Management would feel pressure to justify this arena system after launch, but its weak strategic fit and likely overlap with other sports-floor offerings raise the chance of discontinuation above retention.

This chevron parquet line is close to the core business, highly visible from its home-page presentation, and strongly aligned with the firm’s announced move toward style-oriented natural flooring, so commitment to it should remain high.
A niche squash-court surface finish has limited visibility and narrower strategic relevance, so despite some reluctance to abandon the launch, management is likely to cut it first.

Because this sports-floor accessory is easier to remove than a main flooring system and is not central to the firm’s public direction, escalation of commitment is weaker and withdrawal is slightly more likely than continuation.
